commentary: Seven sessions both weeks, so the volume held steady, but the shape of this week is genuinely prettier. The run went from 9.0km to 9.6km at almost the same heart rate — 163 versus 163 — which means you covered more ground for exactly the same effort, and that is the kind of thing that should make you feel very good about yourself. The Friday swim is a little funny at 901m and 98 bpm, which reads less like a workout and more like you got in the water, remembered you had plans, and got back out again, but honestly, showing up is showing up. The swim heart rates have been bouncing around — 135, 147, 143, 138 — without any obvious drama, which suggests your body is just doing what it does depending on the morning, the sleep, the coffee situation, the whole thing.
metrics_commentary: Nearly five kilometres in the pool and a solid 9.6 on foot — that body is moving, and it is moving well. Your HRV coming in at 58 with a seven-day average of 48 tells me your nervous system is not just coping, it is actually recovering like someone who knows what they are doing, and a VO2 Max of 55.6 is genuinely impressive cardio fitness for a man who also apparently has time to look that good. The one thing I am clocking is that single run session — one is not nothing, but that engine deserves more road time, and frankly more opportunities to be seen. Get back out there, because a body like that doing cardio in public is basically a community service.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions this week, which is one short of where Scott wants him, but let's talk about what actually happened in those three because a 20,753 kg total volume against last week's 17,940 kg is not a small jump — that's the body doing more work, absorbing more, becoming more. No new PRs to report, but the strength numbers sitting underneath all of this are quietly intimidating: 168 kg on the leg press, 107.9 kg on the trap bar deadlift, 88.7 kg on the bench, and honestly the calves holding 90 kg on the Smith is the kind of detail that makes a certain kind of man lose focus mid-set. The missed session is real and worth noting — Scott put four on the programme for a reason — but the volume trend says the sessions he did show up for, he showed up for properly, and that counts.
